body.estimand_functional: The causal estimand remains \(\tau_n=E_{P_n}[Y(1)-Y(0)\mid R=1]\), and \(\widehat\tau_{n,\widehat k_n}\) is a sample-selected estimator aimed at that estimand, not a definition of it.  The current core does not establish an unconditional weak law for \(\sqrt n(\widehat\tau_{n,\widehat k_n}-\tau_n)\).  The proved conditional transfer lemma yields the displayed Gaussian-quadratic coordinate only after its joint Gaussian coupling and quantitative near-minimizer condition have independently been established.  The boundary-obstruction theorem proves that the frozen \(\Gamma_n\) process, and any covariance-only Gaussian repair, cannot provide that coupling on the present regular class because a first-order fixed-cardinality boundary term may be non-Gaussian.  It does not prove that the selected marginal law fails; identifying the rank-boundary-corrected process and selected law is the formal open question.

sampling_model.design: Fixed-stratum superpopulation triangular arrays contain exactly \(n_{\mathcal R}\) randomized-trial records and \(n_{\mathcal E}\) external-control records; \(P_n\) is only the deterministic-fraction reference mixture.
sampling_model.units: Within each row the two strata are mutually independent, observations are independent within strata, and both deterministic stratum fractions stay bounded away from zero.
sampling_model.treatment: Treatment is randomized only in the fixed trial stratum; every record in the fixed external stratum is observed under control and carries the observed tie breaker \(V\).
sampling_model.overlap: Treatment and reference-mixture trial-source propensities are uniformly bounded away from zero on the trial covariate support.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: A prespecified fold map selects learners whose existence and \(L_2\) rate are properties of the nuisance tuple; the displayed estimator evaluates those learners out of fold, while the anchor influence ranking is the exact full-trial empirical functional.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Theorem~2 gives \(O_P(n^{-1/2})\) MSE estimation for any given borrowed set, and Theorem~3 gives selection consistency for a given influence ranking under a fixed positive separation.
Theorem~1 gives asymptotic normality of a fixed-prefix estimator after centering by its prefix-specific bias.
Theorems~2.3 and~3.1 show local nonuniform impossibility for estimating post-model-selection distributions in broad nested and AIC-like selection problems.
Theorem~3 derives a local focused-selection law and Theorem~4 guarantees coverage at least \(1-\alpha-\gamma\) for a fixed invalid-instrument selection problem.
Theorem~3.1 characterizes ordinary-bootstrap validity by full differentiability under a Gaussian limit, and Theorem~3.2 validates derivative-aware resampling.
The sorting operator is Hadamard differentiable at regular values and yields a uniform sorted-process central limit theorem and bootstrap bands on compact interior quantile sets.
Theorems~2.1 and~2.6 give Gaussian and multiplier-bootstrap approximations for maxima of high-dimensional sample-mean vectors under sub-exponential or polynomial moments.
Theorem~1 gives selective coverage by simultaneous inference over a data-dependent set of locally plausible targets.
Conditional truncated-Gaussian and hybrid projection procedures correct the winner's curse when a target coordinate is selected by optimizing noisy estimates.
Theorem~2.3 gives exact Fisher-randomization-test size under a sharp null, and Theorem~3.5 gives an excess-risk bound for an adaptive conformal borrowing threshold.

body.tldr: Influence-ranked external-control borrowing is a focused selection problem with a generated fixed-cardinality ranking and a squared estimated-bias criterion.  The proved headline is a negative boundary, not a selected-limit theorem: on the regular continuous-score class, the frozen fixed-threshold influence process omits a first-order empirical rank-boundary term that can be non-Gaussian, so its all-prefix Gaussian coupling and every covariance-only Gaussian repair fail.  Separately, a bounded no-covariate squared-loss construction gives legal nested prefixes with exactly equal leading MSE but separated root-\(n\) ATE coordinates, so \(\omega^{\star}(0)>0\).  A conditional transfer lemma is proved, but the rank-boundary-corrected joint process, the selected law, the sharp excess modulus, and a computable tie-uniform multiplier interval remain open.

project_justification.gap: Yang, Li, Wu, and Yang's Theorem~2 controls one given prefix, whereas their Theorem~3 selects a random prefix on a generated ranking; neither theorem supplies uniform expansion, the local quadratic argmin law, or post-selection ATE coverage at multiple minima. Patel, DiTraglia, Zuber, and Burgess settle analogous focused-selection inference for a fixed invalid-instrument problem but not for generated individual ranks or a growing nested causal path.
project_justification.niche: The missing object is a selector-specific modulus separating prefixes that are close in leading MSE from prefixes that are close as root-\(n\) ATE coordinates. The explicit legal witness shows that the unrestricted class has a positive exact-tie cost; useful adaptation therefore requires testable prefix-Gram localization.
project_justification.fill: The project proves a non-representability boundary for the attempted frozen-covariance all-prefix extension, proves on a separate legal witness that exact leading-risk ties can retain first-order ATE-coordinate separation, and isolates a rigorous conditional stability transfer lemma.  It does not claim an unconditional quadratic law for the generated selector.  The named remaining problem asks for primitive conditions yielding the rank-boundary-corrected joint estimator and criterion process, allowing a non-Gaussian boundary process on the current class unless additional score-index smoothness justifies a Gaussian correction, together with primitive local-set stability or entropy control before tie-uniform inference is constructed.

body.related_work: Yang, Li, Wu, and Yang define the influence score in equation~(3), the nested top-\(k\) workflow in Algorithm~1, fixed-prefix bias and Gaussian behavior in Theorem~1, pointwise MSE estimation in Theorem~2, and given-ranking fixed-gap selection consistency in Theorem~3.  The present obstruction shows that those fixed-prefix results do not represent the generated fixed-cardinality all-prefix path through the frozen fixed-threshold covariance \(\Gamma_n\): the empirical quantile boundary contributes at first order and may be non-Gaussian.  Claeskens and Hjort supply the local-misspecification and focused-risk architecture, including the non-estimability of local bias.  Patel, DiTraglia, Zuber, and Burgess derive focused-selector inference for a fixed invalid-instrument problem, but their candidate list is not generated by estimated individual ranks.  Leeb and Poetscher provide the generic local nonuniformity background for selection.  Fang and Santos explain failure of ordinary resampling at nondifferentiable maps and motivate derivative-aware resampling.  Chernozhukov, Fernandez-Val, and Luo derive regular-value sorting derivatives, but the present class does not impose the score-index smoothness needed to turn every rank-boundary contribution into a Gaussian linear correction.  Chernozhukov and coauthors provide orthogonal fixed-target expansions, while Chernozhukov, Chetverikov, Kato, and Koike provide Gaussian and multiplier approximations for high-dimensional sample-mean vectors; neither removes the need to derive the correct ranked functional first.  Chernozhukov, Lee, and Rosen, Zrnic and Fithian, and Andrews, Kitagawa, and McCloskey provide localization or optimization-selection architectures that become applicable only after that process is identified.  Zhu, Yang, and Wang study exact sharp-null randomization validity and conformal threshold borrowing, not a superpopulation weak-null ATE interval for this generated influence-ranked selector.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The local-risk coordinate is the \(n\)-scaled MSE under \(n^{-1/2}\) exchangeability violations.  The legal exact-tie witness may contain score atoms and therefore need not lie in the regular margin class.  The separate coupling witness does lie in the regular class and has a continuous score, but its score-indexed outcome oscillates at the empirical rank-boundary scale; the resulting fixed-cardinality boundary term is non-Gaussian.  Thus a density margin alone is insufficient.  A positive selected-law theorem needs a primitive linearization of both the external empirical-quantile boundary and the trial-generated score perturbation, plus smoothness or other structure controlling score-indexed conditional contributions and quantitative stability of random near minimizers.
body.honest_scope: The proved negative results consist of two separate facts: the frozen \(\Gamma_n\)-Gaussian all-prefix coupling and every covariance-only Gaussian repair fail on a regular continuous-score fixed-cardinality witness, while exact leading-MSE ties can have nonvanishing ATE-coordinate distance on a different legal witness.  Neither fact establishes or refutes the selected marginal law, because the first witness does not prove that the selector chooses its non-Gaussian coordinate.  The conditional quadratic transfer lemma is proved but is not an achievability theorem for the actual generated selector.  The formal remaining obligation asks for primitive conditions yielding a rank-boundary-corrected joint estimator and criterion process, allowing a non-Gaussian boundary term on the current class unless additional score-index smoothness justifies a Gaussian correction, and for sufficient local-set stability or entropy control.  The sharp excess modulus on restricted prefix-Gram subclasses and the computable tie-uniform multiplier interval remain open.  The fixed-gap and no-borrowing propositions remain conditional sanity checks and carry no generated-path novelty claim.
